data.title: Moneyfarm rejects eToro's takeover offer - report
data.description:
Trading platform eToro Group's (ETOR) takeover offer for Moneyfarm was rejected by the European digital wealth manager, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

The Israel-based company had offered to buy Moneyfarm for about €250M-€300M, according to the sources, who asked not to be named while discussing private information.

Moneyfarm considered the valuation too low, the sources reportedly noted.

The digital wealth manager's investors include M&G (MGPUF) (MGPFY), Allianz (ALIZF) (ALIZY), Poste Italiane (PITAF), United Ventures, and Cabot Square Capital.

data.title: Baidu and Lyft push ahead with plans for a robotaxi service in London
data.description:
Baidu (BIDU) showed off the company's RT6 autonomous vehicle in London this week as it moves toward launching a driverless robotaxi service in the city in 2027 in partnership with Lyft (LYFT).

Notably, Baidu's (BIDU) robotaxi unit has been testing its sixth-generation RT6 vehicles in London since July in partnership with Freenow by Lyft. The cars started out in the borough of Brent in northwest London, which has a mix of urban and suburban streets, and every test car carries a human safety operator, according to Lyft. Uber said the same day that Apollo Go vehicles were also running on London's public roads under its own separate deal with Baidu. Baidu called this the first time a Chinese self-driving car had been tested in London's traffic. It also followed Baidu's earlier launch in Hong Kong, which, like the UK, drives on the left.

The robotaxis are not meant to replace London's black cabs. Instead, Freenow by Lyft (LYFT) plans a mixed network where robotaxis run alongside its taxis and private-hire drivers.

Baidu (BIDU) is the third robotaxi company in London, after Waymo (WAYMO) and the Uber (UBER)–Wayve partnership.

data.title: Hilltop anticipates 7% to 8% full-year average loan growth in 2026 as deposit costs trend higher
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Hilltop Holdings (HTH) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "For the third quarter, Hilltop reported net income of $24.9 million or $0.44 per diluted share" (President, CEO & Chairman Jeremy Ford). "PlainsCapital Bank further realized growth in core loans and deposits while expanding net interest margin to deliver $44 million in pretax income" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "PrimeLending reported a pretax loss of $11 million as the mortgage market worked through a drastic intra-quarter increase in mortgage rates" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "HilltopSecurities delivered $7 million of pretax income as material interest rate volatility in the quarter pressured the trading business lines at the firm" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

  • "Net interest margin also expanded, increasing over 25 basis points on a year-over-year basis to 3.49%, driven by stable deposit costs and upward repricing of our loan portfolio" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "We expect there to be upward pressure on deposit costs going forward" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

  • "During the quarter, PlainsCapital Bank saw an increase in deposit balances of $500 million" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "In the fourth quarter, we anticipate deposit balance to continue to seasonally expand" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "Notably, PlainsCapital Bank increased deposits swept over from HilltopSecurities during the third quarter by $100 million" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

  • "In total, the mark-to-market losses capturing both rate and volume impacts that are reflected in the third quarter equated to approximately $16 million on a pretax basis" (Executive VP & CFO William Furr). "Hilltop's reported negative AOCI impact equated to approximately $21 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "The quarter also included net valuation gains of $4.6 million related to Hilltop's merchant banking portfolio investments" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "Hilltop maintains strong capital levels with a common equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 18.3%" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "Our tangible book value per share realized a modest quarter-over-quarter decline to $32.20" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "During the quarter, we returned $33 million to stockholders, consisting of $12.6 million in dividends and $20 million in share repurchases" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

Outlook

  • "Our current internal rate outlook anticipates one additional 25 basis point rate increase in 2026" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Under this rate scenario, we expect that NII levels will continue to move modestly higher, largely driven by expected loan growth within our Banking segment" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "We do expect that interest-bearing deposit yields have reached their trough levels for the cycle and will likely trend higher with short-term market interest rates over time" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "We would expect to see NIM level out and potentially travel a little lower from these levels from the 3.33% level" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s rate scenario of "one rate increase to occur in December of 2026" (Executive VP & CFO Furr, Q2), management in Q3 said the market "decidedly" shifted toward "higher short-term interest rates" (Executive VP & CFO Furr) and reiterated an expectation for "upward pressure on deposit costs" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

Financial Results

  • "Net interest income in the third quarter equated to $122 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "During the third quarter, net interest margin increased versus the second quarter of 2026 by 12 basis points to 333 basis points" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "Total noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 equated to $187 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Mortgage revenues declined by $9 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr), and "lock volume" in the quarter "declined 18% to $2.2 billion" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Gain on sale margins for loans sold to third parties declined 26 basis points to 200 basis points" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "Noninterest expenses declined from the same period in the prior year by $7.8 million to $264 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Looking forward, we expect that expenses other than variable compensation will remain relatively stable at current levels" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "Hilltop's allowance for credit losses increased during the quarter by $9 million to $94 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr), and "NPA levels have declined from the second quarter of 2026 by $2 million to $60 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Net charge-offs for the quarter equated to $1.2 million or 6 basis points of the overall loan portfolio" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

Q&A

  • Hannah Wynn, KBW: "Just curious how we should think about the puts and takes" in mortgage and whether to expect "continued losses" or expense reductions; Executive VP & CFO Furr: "we remain focused on productivity and adjusting the business to the current market environment" and "we're going to do everything in our power to drive toward profitability, but also support our LOs across the country".

  • Hannah Wynn, KBW: "Can you just talk about how much runway you still see" on NIM as deposit competition rises; Executive VP & CFO Furr: "we do continue to feel comfortable and confident in kind of the trajectory of NII" and "we would expect to see NIM level out and potentially travel a little lower".

  • Matt Olney, Stephens: asked if strong loan growth can continue into 2027 and about potential payoffs; Executive VP & CFO Furr: "the pipelines remain robust" and "nothing outsized expected in the fourth quarter".

  • Matt Olney, Stephens: asked why repurchases slowed and remaining authorization; President, CEO & Chairman Ford: "the stock price was elevated" and "we saw rates climbing and knew that they have an implication on AOCI," adding "We've got $85 million of authorization left" and "we will be available to transact when the window opens".

  • Evan Yee, Raymond James: asked what drove the improved nonvariable expense outlook and next-year framing; Executive VP & CFO Furr: "we're very pleased we've been able to keep our expenses other than variable compensation stable" and "we believe expenses will be a little lower".

  • Evan Yee, Raymond James: asked about deposit growth into 2027; Executive VP & CFO Furr: "we continue to be focused on growing low-cost and core granular deposits" and "we see a positive trajectory in deposits, I think, going into 2027" while adding "we'll update that guidance as we roll into the January meeting".

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative, centering questions on mortgage profitability and how long pressure persists, including Wynn’s focus on "continued losses" and Yee’s probing on 2027 deposit growth.

  • Management tone was neutral to slightly positive on banking momentum, while more cautious on rate-driven volatility: Furr said "we do not anticipate any significant systemic risk across the portfolio" and Ford emphasized repurchase "prudence" given AOCI sensitivity.

  • Versus the prior quarter, management language shifted from a "muted start" in mortgage (President, CEO & Chairman Ford, Q2) to a sharper rate shock narrative in Q3, with Furr describing "substantial valuation adjustments" and Ford highlighting "drastic" rate increases.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Profitability declined quarter over quarter as management reported Q3 net income of $24.9 million vs. Q2 net income of $36.5 million (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

  • PrimeLending deterioration was a central change, moving from a Q2 pretax loss of $2 million to a Q3 pretax loss of $10.8 million (President, CEO & Chairman Ford), which management tied to September’s rapid rate move and hedge ineffectiveness.

  • Banking commentary remained constructive in both quarters on pipeline/recruiting, while Q3 added more explicit deposit-cost pressure: Q2 noted deposit costs were declining and NIM "will moderate" (Executive VP & CFO Furr, Q2), while Q3 said deposit yields hit a "trough" and will "trend higher" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

Risks and Concerns

  • "There continues to be volatility in the interest rate markets" (Executive VP & CFO Furr) was framed as a primary driver of valuation marks in mortgage and broker-dealer trading, with Furr noting "hedge ineffectiveness" during the quarter.

  • Credit risk monitoring was reiterated amid macro uncertainty: "ongoing conflict in the Middle East, midterm elections and other issues that could contribute to credit risk" (Executive VP & CFO Furr), alongside the mitigation approach of monitoring for "early detection and aggressive workout when necessary" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • Mortgage affordability constraints were described as persistent: "homeowners insurance, property taxes and entry-priced inventory, continue to stress volumes" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford), and Furr added, "we believe that these issues will negatively impact mortgage sales activity into 2027".

Final Takeaway

Management positioned Q3 as a quarter where PlainsCapital Bank’s loan/deposit growth and higher net interest income were offset by interest-rate volatility that drove mortgage and broker-dealer valuation losses and a larger credit provision. Into year-end, management emphasized an outlook for modestly higher net interest income on loan growth, while expecting deposit costs to rise and NIM to level out and potentially move lower, alongside continued efforts to rightsize PrimeLending and sustain capital returns within market and AOCI constraints.

data.title: Vitec highlights 15% sales growth while adding two acquisitions entering Q4
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Vitec Software Group AB (VITBF) Q3 2026

Management View

  • CEO Olle Backman framed Q3 as steady execution, saying, "the highlights for the quarter, of course, continued to grow at 15% in total sales" and adding that "EBITDA also up 15%" while "cash EBIT... was up 13%."

  • Backman emphasized business mix stability and customer concentration, stating, "the 10 largest customers only account for 7% of sales. So that gives us a great risk distribution."

  • On M&A, Backman said, "we didn't sign anything specifically in Q2 or Q3, but in the early days of Q4... we signed... ZMartek and then... AtermIT software," describing ZMartek as "an add-on acquisition" and AtermIT as "in maternity and postnatal care in Netherlands, roughly 16 people."

  • Backman highlighted product “moats” in vertical software and the monetization angle around integration layers, saying, "we are increasingly sort of finding the business models, how to monetize" APIs and ecosystem access.

  • No CFO remarks were included in the Q3 2026 transcript, and no other senior executive besides CEO Olle Backman spoke during prepared remarks.

Outlook

  • Management did not provide explicit revenue, EPS, or formal forward guidance ranges in the Q3 2026 transcript; Backman characterized performance as "fairly roughly in line with our own internal expectations" and said, "we continue to be ready to acquire. We have a good amount of cash and the funding is available, and we are continuing to explore new opportunities there."

  • On R&D scalability over a multi-year horizon, Backman said, "we are seeing increased efficiency in R&D for sure" and added, "spending in absolute terms, probably roughly the same... So in percentages, it's -- over time, it should ideally go down a bit."

  • Compared with Q2’s commentary about demand and momentum building, Q3’s outlook language centered more on activity showing up in transaction-based revenue, with Backman saying, "it is one of these signs that we see that the economy is picking up."

Financial Results

  • Backman summarized Q3 performance as "continued to grow at 15% in total sales," with "EBITDA also up 15%" and "cash EBIT... up 13%," and said, "all in all, a very solid quarter, continued to grow for the third consecutive quarter this year."

  • On year-to-date trends, Backman stated, "on the year-to-date basis, we're 13% up on sales and -- or 14% up on cash EBIT."

  • On cash flow, Backman said it was "a bit better than the corresponding quarter last year" and "roughly SEK 60 million up on the year-to-date," reiterating seasonality from the model: "we basically have all of the cash flow in our first quarter, and then they are pretty flattish on both Q2, Q3 and Q4."

  • On organic growth components, Backman said, "when we look at the subscription base... It's another 4%, the same as last quarter," and added, "the pro forma organic... is actually encouraging up to 6%." He also said, "Another 15% increase in the transaction based, also the same as last quarter."

Q&A

  • Viktor Högberg, Danske Bank: "starting with the transactions revenue... I would assume this is by Enova. Is that right?" CEO Backman: "It's based on a lot of things" including "real estate... really picked up" and Autonet variability, adding, "Enova as well... given the high energy prices and the volatility in the energy market... Enova is always depending on the energy market."

  • Högberg, Danske Bank: "the non-Enova part... seems to be broad-based improved demand" CEO Backman: "It is broad-based. It's really sort of across" and linked it to "increased sort of activity in the general economy."

  • Högberg, Danske Bank: "the pro forma organic growth was higher... What assets are driving that?" CEO Backman: "NMG, Infometric and Autonet are sort of included in the pro forma and those 3 are growing sort of above the group average."

  • Thomas Nilsson, Nordea: transaction-based revenue grew faster than subscriptions and asked "How sustainable" that is. CEO Backman: "it grew 15% also in Q2" and said it is "connected to the drivers in the general economy" while noting, "the housing markets here in the Nordic have been really strong lately."

  • Unknown Analyst (SB1 Markets): asked about "strategic changes... to your management structure." CEO Backman: "hence, the COO role no longer needed because that became the bottleneck itself" and stressed, "We're not changing anything how we operate... from the VPOs and the business units."

  • Unknown Analyst (SB1 Markets): asked whether Q4 seasonality may repeat. CEO Backman: "Not something that we see right now" and added, "it's always hard to predict... It's usually there, but you never know."

  • Högberg, Danske Bank: asked about development spending and tool-driven efficiency. CEO Backman: "we are seeing increased efficiency in R&D for sure" and said outcomes should improve with similar resources.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was neutral to slightly skeptical, repeatedly pressing on transaction revenue drivers and durability, with Nilsson asking "How sustainable do you consider that current growth rate to be?" and SB1 Markets probing timing with "why are you doing this, I mean, as of now?"

  • Management tone was slightly positive and explanatory in prepared remarks ("a very solid quarter") and remained measured in Q&A, repeatedly emphasizing variability and uncertainty in external drivers, including "Enova is always depending on the energy market" and "it's always hard to predict" on seasonality.

  • Versus Q2, Q3 contained less discussion about building order book and more about current activity showing in transactions; Q2 used more forward-leaning language such as "We're cautiously optimistic," while Q3 leaned on steadiness and internal expectations.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 reiterated the same headline growth rate in total sales ("15%"), while cash EBIT growth language softened relative to Q2’s "18% growth" as Q3 cited "cash EBIT... was up 13%."

  • Transaction growth moderated in description from Q2’s "20% growth" and "21% growth in transactional revenues" to Q3’s "15% increase in the transaction based," alongside more explicit linkage to Nordic housing and broader economic activity.

  • M&A narrative shifted from Q2’s "increased activity" but no closes to Q3’s statement that two deals were signed in early Q4: "ZMartek" and "AtermIT."

  • Q2 did not discuss management-structure changes; Q3 introduced the rationale for removing the COO role, with Backman saying, "it is a change in the group management" but not the operating model.

Risks and Concerns

  • Exposure to energy-market volatility remained an explicit swing factor via Enova, with Backman saying, "Enova is always depending on the energy market where that is going."

  • Seasonality and quarter-to-quarter predictability were flagged as uncertain, with Backman noting, "it's always hard to predict" and attributing some seasonality to "budget behaviors from public customers."

  • Transaction-based revenues were described as tied to macro and niche drivers, with Backman saying they are "usually connected to the drivers in the general economy," implying variability versus subscription growth.

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a steady quarter with 15% sales growth and profitability gains, while highlighting that organic subscription growth remained at 4% and transaction-based revenue rose 15% amid stronger Nordic housing activity and broader economic pickup. The call’s most concrete strategic updates were the signing of two acquisitions in early Q4 and an internal management-structure adjustment eliminating the COO role, alongside a measured view that R&D efficiency is improving while absolute spend is expected to remain roughly stable over time.

data.title: Eni set to sign up to $1.8B of infrastructure contracts for Cyprus gas project
data.description:
Eni (E) is poised to sign contracts valued in the $1.3B-$1.8B range for the construction of drilling infrastructure and pipelines at its gas project offshore Cyprus, enabling production to begin in 2028, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

Eni (E) operates the deepwater Cronos field, which it owns with TotalEnergies (TTE) and contains more than 3 Tcf of gas initially in place, and the companies have earmarked the project for fast-tracked development.

Gas will be extracted offshore Cyprus, transported over subsea pipelines to Egypt, where it will be super-cooled and liquefied at the Damietta LNG terminal on the Mediterranean, and then will be loaded and shipped to Europe.

The ability to use existing Egyptian infrastructure in the nearby Egyptian Zohr field, which Cronos borders, makes the project cheaper to deliver, and Eni (E) only needs to construct pipelines to connect the wells to existing pipes in the Egyptian field; an additional pipeline connecting the Zohr gas processing plant to Damietta LNG will also be constructed.

Eni (E) shares rose 4% in Friday's trading after reporting Q3 adjusted EBIT rose 12% Q/Q and doubled Y/Y to €5.99B, including a 76% surge in earnings at its oil and gas unit and a significant increase from refining, while oil and gas production rose 7% Y/Y to 1.83M boe/day.

Q3 adjusted net income more than doubled Y/Y to €2.8B while net cash from operations jumped to €4.36B, both beating analyst estimates, and the company raised its full-year guidance for ​underlying cash flow from operations to €16.5B from €15B, citing strong operational performance and higher commodity prices.

The company said it will pay an extraordinary dividend of ~€1.3B ($1.46B) and increase its share buyback to €3.8B of shares by year-end 2026.

Eni (E) "reported a strong set of results... driven by stronger results in the refining segment ​versus consensus and our expectations, as well as a lower effective tax rate," RBC analyst Biraj ​Borkhataria said in a note.

data.title: Alpine income property trust outlines higher 2026 AFFO of $2.20-$2.22 as acquisitions accelerate
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Alpine Income Property Trust (PINE) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We're pleased to report another strong quarter. AFFO per diluted share grew 19.6% over the third quarter of last year, and we invested approximately $41 million at a weighted average initial yield of 8.5%." (President, CEO & Director John Albright)
  • "Our closed and under contract investments year-to-date now exceed $300 million, a company record that surpasses our full year 2025 total of $277 million." (President, CEO & Director Albright)
  • "Earlier this month announced an agreement to acquire a 13-property industrial portfolio for $117.3 million or approximately $63 per square foot." (President, CEO & Director Albright)
  • "At quarter end, our property portfolio consisted of 130 properties totaling 4.8 million square feet across 31 states with 99.6% occupancy and a weighted average lease term of 8.7 years." (President, CEO & Director Albright)
  • "Third quarter total revenue was $20.5 million, including lease income of $12.8 million and interest income from commercial loan investments of $7.6 million." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Philip Mays)

Outlook

  • "For full year 2026, we are raising our FFO outlook to $2.19 to $2.21 per diluted share, up from $2.10 to $2.13." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)
  • "We are raising our AFFO outlook to $2.20 to $2.22 per diluted share, up from $2.12 to $2.15." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)
  • "Our new guidance ranges reflect our increased investment volume assumption of $310 million to $350 million." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s outlook language, management shifted from raising only "the low end" of guidance to raising the full-year ranges, while increasing the investment volume assumption from "$170 million to $200 million" to "$310 million to $350 million." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays; President, CEO & Director Albright)

Financial Results

  • "FFO and AFFO were both $0.55 per diluted share, up approximately 20% from the third quarter of last year." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)
  • "Second quarter results included approximately $0.02 per diluted share of nonrecurring termination fee income. This quarter did not include any onetime or nonrecurring income." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)
  • "We ended the quarter with net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA of 6.5x." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)
  • "Subsequent to quarter end, we received bank commitments for a new $100 million 4-year term loan and a $75 million increase to our revolving credit facility." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)

Q&A

  • Jay Kornreich, Cantor Fitzgerald & Co.: "[A]ny further details on the industrial portfolio... how you anticipate financing it?" Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays: "We should close on our new financing... a 4-year term loan for $100 million... [and] increase the line $75 million... we go from mid-6s to low 7s, probably 7.3-ish."
  • Jay Kornreich, Cantor Fitzgerald & Co.: "Are you targeting more industrial... or was this transaction... a one-off?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "For right now, it's basically a one-off... we were open to other sectors."
  • Matthew Erdner, JonesTrading: "Do you look to keep [the loan portfolio] at or near 20%?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "It's not a hard set... it could be a situation where the loan book pays down... and we don't replace it to the amount it is now."
  • Matthew Erdner, JonesTrading: "[A]ny credits... you guys may look to move on to... '27?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "We're constantly... pruning... we have some Walgreens left... We have one Sportsman's Warehouse... The Party City in Long Island, we're far along on a lease to replace that."
  • R.J. Milligan, Raymond James: "[A] shift in cap rates...?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "We're going to be targeting sort of that 8 cap plus or minus... this is the time that gets us excited."
  • R.J. Milligan, Raymond James: "[Q]uantify... impact... swap burn off?" Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays: "$100 million will roll up about 150 basis points... the only other swap... is $50 million... closer to market."
  • Michael Goldsmith, UBS: "[B]ridge the moving pieces from the third quarter to the fourth quarter?" Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays: "If you... adjust for... loan activity, it probably falls back to, call it, $0.53 or so... [and] the industrial portfolio... will kind of replace it."
  • Michael Goldsmith, UBS: "[W]hat's the plan to work the leverage down from here?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "[A]sset sales... we have a fair amount of properties with lower cap rate... attributes." Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays: "Dispos will be the biggest mover there."
  • Gaurav Mehta, Alliance Global Partners: "[C]ost of financing... the rate on the term loan?" Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays: "The new term loan has not closed yet... our variable rate debt now is, call it, 5%."
  • Gaurav Mehta, Alliance Global Partners: "[T]iming of $75 million unfunded commitments...?" Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays: "They're really -- it's spread out over a couple of years... the net funding will not be $75 million."
  • Alex Fagan, Baird: "[A]re you assuming to swap that in the fourth quarter?" Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays: "For the new $100 million... term loan, it's already swapped... it will be, call it, 4.75-ish at close."
  • Alex Fagan, Baird: "[A]ny visibility... early prepayments...?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "There's some, but not a material amount."
  • John Massocca, B. Riley Securities: "[I]nvestment volume in the first half of next year...?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "[W]e're basically doing an amount of investment volume this year equal to our market cap... should be less next year."
  • John Massocca, B. Riley Securities: "[I]s this kind of pricing in the new interest rate environment?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "[T]he pricing is somewhat reflecting this new environment of higher interest rates."
  • Craig Kucera, Lucid Capital Markets: "[U]pdate... residential land loans...?" President, CEO & Director Albright: "[T]hey're second home, third home, fourth home sort of communities... we're not worried..." and "[M]ore of a cash pay..." "Exactly."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were largely neutral to slightly negative on balance-sheet and earnings run-rate clarity, pressing on pro forma leverage ("7.3-ish"), fourth-quarter AFFO bridge, and swap roll-offs (Jay Kornreich, Cantor Fitzgerald & Co.; Michael Goldsmith, UBS; R.J. Milligan, Raymond James).
  • Management tone was slightly positive and opportunistic on dealmaking ("this is the time that gets us excited") while staying more guarded on pending-deal specifics ("we haven't closed yet") and near-term loan prepayment visibility ("not a material amount"). (President, CEO & Director Albright; Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)
  • Versus the prior quarter, management’s language placed more emphasis on scaling acquisition volume ("year-to-date now exceed $300 million") and incremental leverage tolerance tied to near-term funding, rather than dividend actions highlighted previously. (President, CEO & Director Albright)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance language shifted from "increasing the low end" in Q2 to "raising" both full-year FFO and AFFO ranges in Q3, alongside a higher stated investment volume assumption (Q2: "$170 million to $200 million"; Q3: "$310 million to $350 million"). (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)
  • Strategic emphasis broadened from a largely net-lease retail focus to a described "one-off" industrial portfolio due to "attractive initial yield" and long duration ("no expiration before late 2031"). (President, CEO & Director Albright)
  • Analyst focus rotated from Q2’s questions on dividend rationale and credit watch items to Q3’s concentration on industrial acquisition financing, leverage trajectory, and swap resets. (Multiple analysts)

Risks and Concerns

  • "Industrial is not a strategic focus" and the pending acquisition remained subject to "customary closing conditions," leaving timing-dependent execution risk into mid-Q4. (President, CEO & Director Albright)
  • Management flagged loan-related earnings variability tied to repayments and rate resets: "the timing of fundings and repayments can cause the relative size of the loan portfolio to vary from quarter-to-quarter." (President, CEO & Director Albright)
  • Interest-rate risk into 2027 was framed around swap resets: "$100 million will be replaced with swaps fixing SOFR at 3.54%." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer Mays)

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized that record year-to-date investment activity and a pending $117.3 million industrial portfolio were key drivers behind raised 2026 FFO and AFFO guidance ranges, while the Q&A concentrated on how incremental debt capacity, asset sales, and swap roll-offs could shape leverage and the near-term AFFO run rate as loan repayments and acquisition timing move results quarter to quarter.

data.title: Kalshi pitches a futures market tied to inflation - report
data.description:
Prediction markets company Kalshi (KALSHI) is pushing further into the territory of traditional financial exchanges by promoting a futures market tied to inflation, according to a media report on Friday.

The company, whose prediction markets platform has surged in popularity, targets launching exchange-traded futures contracts tracking the consumer price index and the closely watched core inflation measure in December, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Kalshi (KALSHI) has been marketing the idea to the world's largest banks and hedge funds, the report said.

The new contracts would be the only futures linked directly to the CPI, offering Kalshi a unique product to attract macro investors active in the multitrillion-dollar markets for interest-rate and bond futures currently offered by CME Group (CME) and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the article said.

The company has called on Michael Ashton, a former Barclays (BCS) trader known as the "Inflation Guy," to design the contracts and pique big investment firms' interest.

"There’s no exchange that trades this, and they want to be the inflation exchange," Ashton, the managing principal of Enduring Investments LLC, told Bloomberg.

data.title: CVS Caremark, Express Scripts, Optum Rx targeted in House investigation
data.description:
• The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform has launched an investigation into whether CVS Caremark (CVS), Express Scripts, and Optum Rx engaged in punitive audits against independent pharmacies as punishment for supporting legislation to reform the pharmacy benefit manager industry.
  • "In the short span of time since the Committee’s July markup of H.R. 6610, the Pharmacists Fight Back in FEHB Plans Act, multiple independent pharmacies that supported the Committee’s efforts have received an unusual number of audit notices for minuscule prescription charges after the stated compliance deadline date from CVS Caremark," Chairman James Comer (R-Ky.) writes in his letter to CVS Caremark.
  • One audit conducted by a PBM was over a drug that cost $0.99 "that resulted in hundreds of hours of staff time for the independent pharmacy," according to a news release.
  • Comer is asking for information from the three PBMs related to audits conducted from July 22 to the present.
  • Express Scripts is owned by Cigna (CI), while Optum Rx is a part of UnitedHealth (UNH).
